# PERF_SWEEP — `run_backtest` event-loop profile + bit-identical optimizations

Scope: ULTRAPLAN P4.1 (profile + classify the remaining event-loop gap) and
P6.8 (top-20 hot paths; fix only where semantics are provably bit-identical).

**All workloads below are SYNTHETIC** — generated by
`tests/perf/synthetic.py::daily_ohlcv` (`source="synthetic"` bars). They are
correctness/performance tests only, never market evidence.

## Workload

- `daily_ohlcv(n_symbols=11, n_days=1000)` — 11 assets × 1000 daily bars
  (11 000 rows), plus `adv = close*volume` and `vol_20 = 0.02` columns, the
  same panel idiom as `tests/perf/test_benchmarks.py`.
- Weights: SMA-20 gate replaying `scripts/_bench_fast.py::load_workload` —
  sid gets `0.9/n` when `close[i] > mean(close[i-19:i+1])` else `0.0`, rows
  for every sid every day from `i ≥ 19` (10 791 weight rows).
- Config: permissive `RiskGateConfig`, `commission_bps=10.0`
  (`scripts/_perf_sweep.py::make_cfg`). 6 517 orders result.
- Instrument: macOS arm64, Python 3.12.14, polars 1.44.2, numpy 2.5.3,
  numba 0.67.0. cProfile only — py-spy/scalene are not installed in this env
  and no new heavy deps were added; tracemalloc covers the allocation trace.

`scripts/_perf_sweep.py` reproduces: `uv run python scripts/_perf_sweep.py`.
`scripts/_perf_identity.py` reproduces the before/after byte-identity replay:
`uv run python scripts/_perf_identity.py --reps 7`.

Gone from the top-20: `market_risk_overlay_asof` /
`resolve_market_variance_overlay_asof` / `realized_garch_*` / `Path.exists` /
`posix.stat` (38 ms cumulative — hoisted), scalar `_valid_price` (31 ms —

1.9 µs → 1.2 µs/call.

## What was optimized (all provably bit-identical)

| Change | Why identical |
|---|---|
| `_valid_price` per-row scalar checks → `_valid_price_lists` vectorized masks (`np.isfinite(arr) & (arr > 0)` on `Float64`/`Float32` columns; scalar fallback otherwise) | Selection only — no arithmetic. `to_numpy()` maps null→NaN, and `isfinite & >0` reproduces the float branch exactly; `Float32`→`float64` widening is exact. |
| `day_rows_map` row-dicts → `day_idx_map` row-index lists + column arrays (`sid_l`, `open_v/open_ok`, `close_v/close_ok`, `close_total_return`, `adv_v/adv_ok`, `vol_v/vol_ok`) | Same values in same order; kills ~22k row-dict builds. |
| `weights_by_date` + `_target_weight_map` via unnamed `iter_rows()` + column-index map | Same `(event_time, security_id) → weight` entries, identical ValueError texts and duplicate-key detection order. |
| `market_risk_overlay_asof`/`resolve_market_variance_overlay_asof` per-day calls → `overlay_possible` flag hoisted before the loop (`_garch_artifact_path().exists() or _realized_garch_artifact_path().exists()`) | When no artifact exists both calls return `(None, None)` side-effect-free — the 2 `Path.exists` stats/day were pure overhead. Precedent: `_fast_replay_is_complete` already probes artifact existence once at dispatch. Caveat: a spec artifact *created mid-run* is now ignored (old code would pick it up) — pathological race, documented. |
| `_projected_exposures`: drop `dict(book.shares)` copy; iterate `share_ids \| {sid}` instead of `set(projected) \| set(prices)` | A mark-only id never contributes (projected qty 0 fails the filter), so the scanned set is identical post-filter; summation order (sorted contributors) unchanged. Caller threads `share_ids` incrementally (`add` on the only mutation site). |
| `sum(genexpr)` → `sum(listcomp)` / `sum(map(abs, ...))`; `Book.nav` list-comp over `prices.get` | Identical summation sequence — Python `sum()` semantics preserved (no np.float64 terms introduced; see FAST_REPLAY_P42 float-safety rule). |

## Rejected (not provably bit-identical)

- Vectorizing per-order `total_cost` / `check_order` / `_make_order`:
  sequential book dependency (each order mutates shares/cash consumed by the
  next), per-call fail-closed validation is the contract, and `Order` is a
  pydantic schema. These are the remaining bulk: `total_cost` 54 ms,
  `check_order` 27 ms, `_make_order`+pydantic ~22 ms instrumented.
- `np.sum`-style pairwise reductions for `gross`/`net`/`Book.nav`: pairwise
  summation differs from Python `sum()` at the ulp level.
- Cross-order batching of fills or gates: changes fill ordering.

## Before/after timings (7-rep median, same process)

| Path | Before | After | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_run_backtest_event_loop` | 166.2 ms | 117.8 ms | **1.41×** |
| `run_backtest` auto-dispatch (fast replay) | 22.4 ms | 22.4 ms | unchanged — different kernel |
| `run_backtest_fast` pinned | 20.4 ms | 22.8 ms | unchanged |

## Byte-identity evidence

`scripts/_perf_identity.py` loads the pre-change `engine.py` from git via
`git show origin/main:...` into an isolated module (the
`_bench_before_after.py` idiom) and replays both engines on seven workloads:
headline `sma11x1000`, `sparse_delist` (missing opens/nulls/delisted name),
`close_auction_fill`, `kill_halt`, `frictionless`, `tight_gate_rejects`,
`int_price_fallback` (non-float price column → scalar fallback path). For
each: `equity` and `fills` Arrow IPC bytes equal, normalized metrics digest
equal (or identical exception — `StaleValuationError` with identical args).

```
  sma11x1000:          equity/fills/metrics byte-identical
  sparse_delist:       equity/fills/metrics byte-identical
  close_auction_fill:  equity/fills/metrics byte-identical
  kill_halt:           equity/fills/metrics byte-identical
  frictionless:        equity/fills/metrics byte-identical
  tight_gate_rejects:  identical exception StaleValuationError
  int_price_fallback:  equity/fills/metrics byte-identical
event_loop before: 166.2 ms median / after: 117.8 ms median — 1.41x
sweep workload equity sha256 (both engines): 6abf3466…6b35ec7c
```

**Pre-existing divergence (not this change):** the property suite's
`test_fast_replay_byte_identical_on_generated_workloads` and
`test_interpreted_fallback_byte_identical` fail on `_gen_workload(seed=0)`
on `origin/main` too (verified by replaying the unmodified engine — the
fast replay path diverges from the event loop there). This PR's evidence is
old-vs-new event loop identity, which holds on all 20 property seeds
(18 byte-identical, 2 identical `StaleValuationError`s) plus the seven
workloads above. Fixing the fast-replay divergence is out of scope.

Digest caveat: `aggregate_shortfall`'s `by_side`/`top_cost_names` are polars
`group_by` float sums whose parallel partition order is nondeterministic at
the ulp level even on an identical input frame (verified: same frame
aggregated twice yields different ulps — pre-existing property, not this
change). The digest therefore replaces those lists with sorted
`(key, n_fills)` membership pairs; every other metric field compares
bit-exact, including `implementation_shortfall` top-level totals.

## P4.1 — classification of the remaining gap

Event loop now ~118 ms vs fast replay ~22 ms (≈5.3× residual, vs ~5.4×
before). Decomposition of the remaining event-loop time:

- **Per-order gate/cost semantics** (~80%): `total_cost` + `check_order` +
  `_make_order` + pydantic `Order` validation + `sqrt_impact` — sequential
  per-order contract work; not vectorizable without changing semantics.
- **Interpreter loop body** (~15%): bookkeeping dict comprehensions,
  `sorted(ids)`, nav/turnover accounting.
- **Polars marshalling** (~5%): `iter_rows` residue + `_build_result` frames.

The residual gap is the product: per-order fail-closed risk gates and
order-schema validation — exactly the semantics the fast replay path
satisfies through its pre-validated vectorized kernel.
